q1fy27.text: June rainfall deficit 23% of LPA, moderating to 17% by the call; all-India reservoirs 34% of capacity vs 57% a year earlier, southern reservoirs 28% vs 65%.

Kharif NBS raised ~10% for N, P, S but 'without factoring the Middle East crisis'; rates 'do not fully compensate' input costs. Industry seeking a review; further MRP increases 'not doable'. Industry raised prices 25-30% across grades.

Phosphoric acid settled at $1,700/t for Q2 vs $1,360 in Q1 (and $1,290 before). Sulphur 'holding high' (structural demand from nickel leaching); own acid makes sense with sulphur up to ~$800/t at a $1,700 acid price.

Production deliberately cut to 6.9 lakh t (72% utilisation) from 8.4 lakh t; new sulphuric and phosphoric acid plants at Kakinada commissioned and stabilising (60% of acid needs now in-house); granulation expansion (7.5 lakh t) on track for Q4FY27.
DAP+NPK volumes -9% to 10.1 lakh t; primary market share 22% (18%); point-of-sale volume +13% to 7.9 lakh t (16% share); SSP +19%, >50% differentiated grades.

Standalone revenue +20% to ₹870 cr, EBIT +44% to ₹159 cr (record quarter) on exports/B2B and price pass-through; NACL revenue ₹383 cr, EBITDA ₹41 cr (11% margin, from 8%); NACL margin 'reasonable level' — further gains need new products over 2-3 years.

~₹7,000 cr invested over the last 3-4 years (organic and inorganic); next 1-2 years focus on returns; 'normal sustainable capex of ₹300 crores'. No new fertiliser capacity immediately; CP spare AI capacity at NACL.

Fertiliser EBITDA to rise from ~₹5,000/t to ₹6,500/t at steady state after backward integration ('don't ask me this number for this quarter'); specialty nutrients growing 25-30% at ~20% EBITDA margin; SSP ₹2,500-3,000/t.
Q1 D&A ₹203 cr (₹121 cr a year earlier): PA-SA plants +₹16-18 cr, NACL acquisition intangibles ~₹20-21 cr, Senegal mine overburden amortisation ~₹30 cr.
Subsidy outstanding ₹3,254 cr at 30-Jun-2026 (₹568 cr received in July); subsidy business 77% of revenue, 48% of EBITDA in Q1. Rupee traded ₹92.6-96.8/$ in Q1.

q4fy26.text: Record fertiliser production 3.5 mt; DAP+NPK sales 4.3 mt (+7%); 17.5% consumption share; SSP 8.4 lakh t; retail +30%; nano ~45 lakh bottles; combined crop protection ~₹4,000 cr; NACL FY26 revenue ₹1,585 cr (+28%), EBITDA ₹103 cr.
Manufactured fertiliser EBITDA 'around ₹5,000 plus' per tonne in FY26, below ₹3,500 in Q4FY26; trading margin ~4-5%.

India depends >80% on imports for ammonia and sulphur, most crossing the Strait of Hormuz; ammonia ~$840-850/t and sulphur ~$800/t in May-2026. Q1 raw materials covered; trading (DAP) volumes may fall in FY27.
Standalone growth of 20-25% plus capacity-led AI growth; ~19% margin sustainable; currency depreciation helps exports; 20,000 t mancozeb expansion at Sarigam by mid-2026.

Note 31.6: the company awaits clarity on the government's new 'reasonable margin' guidelines (a cap on profit from subsidised P&K fertilisers) and continues normal segment disclosure. A binding cap would limit the upside from backward integration.

NACL purchase-price allocation adds ~₹80 cr a year of intangible amortisation and a 46% minority; BMCC mine amortisation sits in D&A, not EBITDA, so EBITDA overstates cash profit from Senegal less than D&A suggests.
FY25 profit includes a ₹397.71 cr land-rights gain; FY26 includes a ₹70.56 cr drone goodwill impairment (inside segment profit) and FY25 a ₹50.94 cr asset impairment.
Trade payables of ₹8,827 cr include ₹5,022 cr of acceptances (bank-backed supplier credit, mostly for imported raw materials); interest on these runs through finance cost.
